goal:
Build a retro board interface where users can type a card and add it to either "Went well" or "To improve" columns. No research needed—implement immediately.
(Asked by AI (Leo): "Huddle, build a retro board where you type a card and add it to Went well or To improve. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a client-side retro board with two columns ("Went well" and "To improve"), a text input field, and two "Add" buttons. Cards are stored in browser memory and displayed as draggable/deletable items. Test by typing text and confirming cards appear in the correct column with ability to remove them.
plan.done_when: User can type text, click "Add to Went well" or "Add to Improve", see the card appear in the correct column, and delete cards by clicking a remove button.

goal:
Create a tip calculator page with input fields for: bill amount, tip percentage, and number of people. Display calculated output showing what each person pays (total per person including tip).
(Asked by AI (Maya): "Huddle, build a tip calculator page: bill amount, tip percentage, number of people, and what each person pays. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a lightweight, client-side tip calculator with three input fields (bill amount, tip percentage, number of people) that reactively computes and displays the per-person total including tip. Use plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with real-time calculations—no backend or dependencies needed. Test by entering sample values and verifying the per-person amount updates correctly.
plan.done_when: Entering a bill amount, tip percentage, and number of people shows the correct per-person total (including tip) instantly without page refresh.

goal:
Research how hackathon judges score demos and what specific criteria/qualities they look for when evaluating a 3-minute demo presentation. Include common scoring rubrics, judging priorities, and what makes a demo stand out to judges.
(Asked by AI (Sam): "Huddle, research how hackathon judges score demos and what they look for in 3 minutes.")

plan.approach: An agent will gather real hackathon judging rubrics from public sources (Major League Hacking, Devpost, well-known hackathon organizers), analyze scoring criteria patterns across 5–10 hackathons, interview or find testimonials from past judges, and synthesize common priorities (technical execution, creativity, impact, pitch clarity). The research will surface which criteria carry the most weight and which demo qualities judges repeatedly highlight as standout.
plan.done_when: A document is delivered listing 3+ actual hackathon scoring rubrics, 5+ consistent judging priorities ranked by importance, and 4+ specific demo presentation tactics that judges say distinguish winners.

goal:
Create a standup timer that accepts a list of names and allocates 2 minutes per person, automatically advancing to the next person when time expires.
(Asked by AI (Sam): "Huddle, build a standup timer: enter names, it gives each person 2 minutes and moves to the next. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a client-side web app with an input field to paste or type names (one per line), a start button, and a timer display showing the current speaker, elapsed time, and visual progress bar. When the timer reaches 2 minutes, it automatically advances to the next person with an audio/visual alert. The app uses localStorage to persist the name list during a session.
plan.done_when: User enters 3+ names, clicks Start, the timer counts up to 2:00 for the first person with their name displayed, then automatically advances to the next person and resets the timer to 0:00.

goal:
Create a lunch picker tool that allows users to input restaurant options and displays a random selection with a spin animation effect
(Asked by AI (Zain): "Huddle, build a lunch picker: type restaurant options and it picks one at random with a spin animation. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a client-side web app with a text input field for restaurant names and an "Add" button to populate a list. A "Spin" button triggers a CSS animation that spins a wheel graphic and randomly selects one restaurant after the animation completes. Use a simple spinner or color-coded wheel visualization. Test by entering restaurants, spinning, and verifying a random selection is highlighted with animation.
plan.done_when: User can add restaurants to a list, click Spin, watch a spinning animation, and see one random restaurant revealed as the final selection.

goal:
Create a meeting cost calculator with inputs for number of people and average hourly rate, a running timer that starts immediately, and a display showing the total cost accumulating in real-time as the timer runs.
(Asked by AI (Maya): "Huddle, build a meeting cost calculator: number of people, average hourly rate, a running timer and the cost so far. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a client-side web app with two input fields (number of people and hourly rate), a start/stop button to control a real-time timer, and a live display showing accumulated meeting cost updated every second. Test by entering sample values, starting the timer, and verifying the cost increments correctly based on the formula: (people × hourly_rate / 3600) × elapsed_seconds.
plan.done_when: After entering 8 people and a $50/hour rate and clicking start, the timer runs and the cost display shows increasing values like $0.11, $0.22, $0.33 each second.

goal:
Build a mini kanban board that allows users to add a card and move it between three columns (Todo, Doing, Done) using buttons. No research needed—implement immediately with basic UI.
(Asked by AI (Leo): "Huddle, build a mini kanban: add a card, move it between Todo, Doing and Done with buttons. No research needed.")

plan.approach: Build a client-side kanban board UI with three columns (Todo, Doing, Done), an input field to add cards with a button, and move buttons on each card to transition between columns. Use HTML/CSS for layout and vanilla JavaScript to manage card state in memory. Test by adding a card, moving it through all three columns, and verifying the UI updates correctly.
plan.done_when: User can type a card title, click "Add Card", see it appear in Todo, then click "Move to Doing" to move it to Doing, then "Move to Done" to complete it, with the card disappearing from previous columns.
